touches.text: It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim.
Any shim, through its pulse.py, brings the bus up if it's down: whatever is called brings up what it needs (5.3.4.1).

pulse.py asks nobody anything. It starts the shim if it's down, else tells the mechanisms inside the shim that need a pulse "here ya go!" Only daemon-shaped things hang there, things that actually need a heartbeat (eg cc's Gmail fetch, 10.3.6); everything else fires on events. WHY: "the point behind the ground loop firing pulse.py was to give you a structure to hang deamons from, not managers."

What the waker starts outlives whoever started it (detached, or through systemd-run --user, which gives it its own memory cap and log while still deciding nothing). Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke.
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.

CC's memory lives in a private git repo of its own, linked into the place Claude Code looks for it on each box, so every CC instance is the same CC whichever box it runs on. Its distillations (the method, and CC's patterns to avoid) are published in the CC device in cairn; how we got there, and anything of CC's history of Akien, stays in the private repo. WHY: cairn and CairnCommons are public. "How Akien does it" is meant for anybody; Akien himself, and the people around him, are not. A memory starts private; only a distillation crosses, and Akien reviews what crosses.
